findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence command field (transition-orchestrator.ts) records grep -n "persistClaim = acquireMkdirLock|store.writeChecklist(args.storyId, reopenChecklist)|store.writeStory(args.storyId, story)|persistClaim.release()" packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts with a bare | for alternation. Default (BRE) grep treats | as a literal character, not alternation, so running the recorded command verbatim produces ZERO output -- not the four matching lines (859/935/937/940) the note claims. Confirmed by running it verbatim in this worktree (no output) vs with -E added (matches all four lines as described). The underlying factual claims in the note are independently verified TRUE (I re-derived the same line numbers, the single REOPEN assignment site at line 651, PHASE_EVENT_BY_TARGET lacking REOPEN, and store.writeJsonFile tmp+rename at store.ts:133-145), so this is not a coverage gap -- it is a reproducibility/hygiene defect in the recorded command string of an otherwise-adequate docs_check evidence entry.
findings.resolvedReason: Re-recorded CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence with a reproducible command: grep -Fn with one -e per literal (replace-in-place confirmed at checklist.ts:934-937; exactly 1 entry, no duplicate). The stored string was extracted back out of checklist.json and executed verbatim: exit 0, exactly the four claimed lines 859/935/937/940. The reviewer-suggested grep -nE does NOT work here (literals contain unescaped parens = ERE metacharacters; ugrep aborts with empty (sub)expression, exit 2), so -F was used as POSIX-portable. Other cited line numbers re-verified, not copied forward.

findings.desc: plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts:266,299,302,314 use 4 unnecessary `as any` casts ((e as any).fromPhase/.toPhase, reopenEvents[0] as any) on the new reopen-persistence + normal-transition-shape assertions. ProcessEvent (core/types.ts) already declares `[key: string]: unknown`, so `e.fromPhase` / `e.toPhase` / `reopenEvents[0].transitionType` resolve to `unknown` without any cast, and `unknown` compares/assigns fine against string literals in assert.equal/hasOwnProperty.call under this project's strict tsconfig. Verified empirically: in an isolated scratch git-worktree copy (separate from the shared REVIEW worktree/dist per the concurrency-hazard note) I removed all 4 casts, ran `npm --prefix packages/main run build` (tsc, strict) -> 0 errors, and reran `node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js` -> both smoke assertions still pass unchanged. So the casts add no compile-time necessity; they just suppress the (already-weak, index-signature-typed) safety net for no benefit. Low severity: test-only file, no behavior difference, `as any` here does not actually widen acceptance beyond what the index signature already allows (a property-name typo would still silently type-check either way) so this is a minor precision/hygiene cleanup rather than a masked-typo risk.
findings.resolvedReason: Removed all 4 unnecessary `as any` casts from plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts (266/299/302/314); ProcessEvent already declares [key: string]: unknown so plain property access type-checks under strict tsconfig. Verified on the real tree: grep -n "as any" returns nothing, build exits 0, plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js and flow-stability-smoke.js both exit 0. Assertions semantically identical.

findings.desc: Cross-host review round B-70a6-xhr-r1/r2: independent host codex-host-b returned decision=fail with one MAJOR finding (recorded here by the main agent for tracking; the authoritative verdict is the host_verdict process event, not this record). Finding: "New reopen audit semantics are absent from the process-fact contract" at packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts:1371. This story makes transitionType and reason durable semantics of PLAN->INIT phase_transition events, but the registered phase-transition process fact still describes only fromPhase/toPhase/attemptId/reviewRound/materialHash/storyFilesHash, and scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs has no assertion for the new fields. That violates the CLAUDE.md dual-layer process-fact contract (prompt guidance + hardcoded mechanical fallback) and lets a later refactor silently drop the reopen marker or the reason while the mechanical contract still passes - defeating the audit guarantee this story exists to establish. Fix: extend the runtime phase-transition process-fact declaration to cover the REOPEN marker + reason semantics, and extend verify-process-fact-contract.mjs to mechanically assert that a successful REOPEN emits transitionType=reopen with the validated reason while ordinary transitions omit both fields. Note: all three local Claude reviewers (concept, quality, test-coverage) passed without catching this; the independent host did.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b964aa7619, addressing the MAJOR finding raised by independent host codex-host-b in cross-host rounds r1/r2. (1) packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts: the runtime:closeout_phase_transition entry now declares the reopen audit semantics - transitionType='reopen' as the backward-reopen marker and reason as the already-validated operator reason (>= REOPEN_REASON_MIN), both strictly additive and set ONLY on REOPEN, with ordinary transitions omitting them. Declared honestly as audit-only history, NOT gate evidence, since nothing currently consumes it; the implementer explicitly declined to over-claim it as gate-consumed. (2) scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs: new assertPhaseTransitionReopenAuditContract(), called beside assertCloseoutTrustBoundary(), following the file's existing registry-token plus AST-anchored source assertion style (source-first by design so a stale dist cannot hide drift). It asserts four layers: the builder emits each field only via a real input.<field> !== undefined spread with an empty else; the call site gates on a real eventType === REOPEN condition emitting exactly transitionType 'reopen' plus args.reason, with an empty object on the ordinary branch; the PLAN->INIT remap keeps a throwing REOPEN_REASON_MIN branch so the persisted reason is the validated one; and the two executable smokes keep their end-to-end assertions. RED PROOF (isolated filesystem copy, deleted afterwards, so the shared worktree git state was never perturbed): scratch baseline exit 0, then 7 mutations each producing exit 1 and each restored - remove the call-site REOPEN gate; drop reason; rename the marker to 'REOPEN'; make the ordinary branch emit undefined fields; make the builder emit transitionType unconditionally; delete the reason validation; revert the registry rationale. For the primary mutation the full path was run: the mutated tree COMPILES CLEAN (npm --prefix packages/main run build exit 0, proving tsc cannot catch this class of regression) while npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 1 with the message that the call site must gate the reopen audit fields on a real eventType === REOPEN condition; reverting flips it back to exit 0, proving the failure is caused by the mutation rather than the scratch environment. Post-change verification on the shared worktree: build exit 0, test:process-fact-contract exit 0 ('Process fact contract verified'), plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke exit 0, flow-stability-smoke exit 0. This closes the dual-layer process-fact gap: the audit guarantee this story establishes can no longer be silently refactored away while the mechanical contract keeps passing.
